## Context / Problem

The local `.github/actions/setup-uv` composite action downloads the uv release with a single anonymous `Invoke-WebRequest` against `https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/<version>/<asset>` and has no retry. When GitHub's release-download edge returns a transient 5xx, the step fails at once and every job that installs uv goes red before it tests anything. Every workflow uses this action, including the per-change `Verified` pipeline.

Observed on the scheduled `Live External Integration` run 42572022074 (2026-11-08 22:16 PST, head `0f409b946e4`): 5 of the 9 setup-uv invocations failed within the same minute with `504 Gateway Time-out The server didn't respond in time.` at the `Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $archive` line (langfuse, jira DC smoke, Pandoc ubuntu, Pandoc macos, live bedrock). In the same minute, 4 other jobs downloaded the identical uv 0.13.6 asset successfully (the openai arm logged `Successfully installed uv 0.13.6 from uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`, 1 second before the langfuse job's 504 on the same asset). GitHub's status feed records the incident "Increased timeouts due to surge in anonymous users" on 2026-11-09 ("high rates of 504 errors for anonymous requests"; "Logged-in users and authenticated requests are unaffected"), plus a related unauthenticated-timeout incident on 2026-11-08. The asset downloads with HTTP 200 now.

The uv version and checksums are not the cause: the 2026-11-02 scheduled run (head `c43d9336262`) already installed uv 0.13.6 through this action and every setup-uv step passed. Change 3291 (`e0ab18822c6`) changed how the action obtains the version string but not the URL, the asset, or the download line that failed.

The bedrock arm's second failure, `Summarize LLM token usage` (`No module named 'rebar'`), is a downstream effect of the same failure: that step runs under `if: always()` and the package was never installed because setup-uv failed.

Found while verifying `unkempt-amaranth-archerfish`.

## Approach

Give the download a bounded retry using PowerShell's built-in `Invoke-WebRequest -MaximumRetryCount 5 -RetryIntervalSec 10`. PowerShell 7 retries the request when it receives a status from 400 to 599 (or 304), waits the interval between attempts, and writes `-OutFile` only for the successful response; the SHA-256 check that follows is unchanged, so a retried download is verified exactly as before. The worst case adds 50 seconds before a persistent failure surfaces, and a persistent error (for example a 404 for a wrong version) still fails the step with the final response.

Why this fits: the failure is a short-lived upstream 5xx on some requests (4 of 9 succeeded in the same minute), which a bounded retry absorbs. It adds no input, env var, config key, or feature flag, and needs no token. Sending the workflow token was considered and rejected: it would add an env var to the step, and a public report of the same incident shows authenticated `releases/download` requests still returning 504.

Portability: the retry lives in the action's own PowerShell command, so it applies on every runner OS the action supports and adds no CI-only trigger.

## Scope

- `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml`: add `-MaximumRetryCount 5 -RetryIntervalSec 10` to the `Invoke-WebRequest` download line, with a one-line comment naming this failure.
- `tests/unit/test_setup_uv_download_retry.py` (new): regression tests for the download command.

## Testing

Written first and run against the unfixed tree to confirm they fail:
- Happy path (structure): `test_setup_uv_download_retries_transient_failures` loads `action.yml` with `yaml.safe_load`, finds the step whose `run` script contains `Invoke-WebRequest`, and asserts the call carries `-MaximumRetryCount` of at least 3 and a `-RetryIntervalSec`. On `origin/main` it fails because the call has neither.
- Behaviour, failure-then-success: `test_setup_uv_download_survives_two_504s` starts a local `http.server` on 127.0.0.1 that answers the first 2 requests with 504 and the third with a fixed payload, extracts the action's `Invoke-WebRequest` line verbatim, runs it under `pwsh` with `$url` pointing at the local server, and asserts the output file equals the payload and the server saw 3 requests. Skipped when `pwsh` is not on PATH (GitHub's ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners ship it, so CI runs it).
- Edge, persistent failure: `test_setup_uv_download_fails_on_persistent_504` uses a server that always answers 504 with the retry interval overridden to 1 second in the extracted line, and asserts `pwsh` exits non-zero and no output file is written. Skipped without `pwsh`.
- The existing `tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` and `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` confirm the action still passes the uv pin gate.

No autouse fixtures and no new shared test helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `Invoke-WebRequest` download in `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml` carries `-MaximumRetryCount 5 -RetryIntervalSec 10`; verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_setup_uv_download_retry.py` passing, after the structural test was observed failing on the unfixed tree.
- [x] The uv pin gate accepts the tree: `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` exits 0 and `pytest tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py` passes.
- [x] `make lint` (with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`) exits 0.
- [x] [non-codebase] The change lands through Gerrit at `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`; the change number and merged SHA are recorded as a ticket comment.
- [x] [non-codebase] A `workflow_dispatch` run of `Live External Integration` on `main` after the merge shows every setup-uv step succeeding; the run id and per-job setup-uv outcomes are recorded as a ticket comment.
